features: 360 degree horizontal pan / 116 degree vertical tilt
abnormal sound detection (glass breaking, meow, bark)
release_notes: Indoor 4K pan/tilt AI camera. Sensor, 4 mm F1.6 lens, full FOV triplet, 4K 8MP resolution, 360/116 degree pan-tilt range, 512 GB microSD limit, and the full AI detection list from the official Tapo product page specification table (Tapo C250_V1 Datasheet), cross-checked against distributor republications of the same table. Frame rate, dimensions, weight, and operating temperature omitted: not recovered from an official source. Night vision stated officially as 40 ft (approx. 12 m).

frigate.notes: Mains-powered Tapo cameras expose RTSP once a Camera Account is created in the Tapo app (Settings > Advanced > Camera Account). /stream1 is the main stream, /stream2 the substream. go2rtc alternative: TP-Link's proprietary protocol via go2rtc (tapo://<tapo-account-password>@{ip}) is often more stable than RTSP (fewer timeouts / non-monotonic-timestamp errors). The password is your Tapo app/cloud account password — not the camera's RTSP/Device account — so all cameras on one account share it; only the IP changes. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). Pan/tilt: Tapo exposes ONVIF PTZ on port 2020 (not 80) — point Frigate's onvif block at host:<ip> port:2020 with the camera Account credentials for manual pan/tilt. (Frigate autotracking stays off: Tapo only does continuous-move ONVIF, no reliable absolute/FOV positioning.)

home_assistant.notes: Native TP-Link Tapo integration. Requires Tapo cloud account credentials.

blue_iris.notes: Use Generic/ONVIF profile. RTSP streams: /stream1 (main), /stream2 (sub). Must enable the Camera Account / ONVIF in the Tapo app.
